name: Revision of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation (proposed)

literature.title: Current developments in consumer protection policy: Review of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation
literature.venue: European Parliamentary Research Service briefing, PE 766.252
literature.method: review of the Commission's 2024 report on the application of the regulation and its supporting study
literature.outcomes: national enforcement capacity, alerts, traders outside the EU, deterrence, procedures
literature.headline: Summarises the Commission's July 2024 report on how the CPC Regulation works: cooperation helps, but national enforcement resources are uneven, authorities lack capacity against digital infringements, alerts are used unevenly and traders outside the EU are hard to reach.
literature.summary_plain: Parliament's research service explains what the Commission found when it reviewed how national consumer authorities work together.
literature.quality: Secondary summary of official findings; no new data.
literature.citation: Ashton, D. (2024), Current developments in consumer protection policy: Review of the Consumer Protection Cooperation Regulation, EPRS briefing PE 766.252, European Parliament

literature.authors: Hausemer, P., Michaelsen, F., Vitić, J., Aumont, L. (VVA); Jeffries, I., Godfrey, E., Heetman, A., Voarino, L. (Tetra Tech); Cordon, A. (Ipsos)
literature.title: Information gathering for assisting the European Commission in complying with its obligations under Article 40 (“reporting”) of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 on Consumer Protection Cooperation: Final report
literature.venue: Study for the European Commission, DG Justice and Consumers (Publications Office, doi:10.2838/569634)
literature.method: evaluation (effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence, EU added value): desk research, three surveys of authorities, alert entities and traders, interviews and six market case studies
literature.outcomes: detection of cross-border infringements, use of enforcement powers, costs for authorities and traders, deterrence, non-EU traders
literature.headline: Evaluation behind the Commission's review: authorities judge the regulation effective and efficient overall, but find it too slow for fast-moving infringements, weakened by sparing use of fines, of little reach against traders outside the EU, and applied unevenly because national powers and resources differ.
literature.summary_plain: A contractor study for the Commission that asked national authorities, consumer groups and companies how well cross-border enforcement works.
literature.quality: Evaluation based mainly on stakeholder views; the study notes that national data are very limited and few traders responded.
literature.verified: full text of the final report read (executive summary and title page)
literature.citation: Hausemer, P. et al. (2024), Information gathering for assisting the European Commission in complying with its obligations under Article 40 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 on Consumer Protection Cooperation, Final report, VVA, Tetra Tech and Ipsos for DG JUST, doi:10.2838/569634
